construct: Renal prostaglandins normally support afferent arteriolar dilation, particularly when effective circulating volume is reduced. Cyclooxygenase inhibition lowers prostaglandin synthesis, causing relative afferent vasoconstriction and reduced glomerular capillary pressure.

notes: Official USMLE Step 1 page verified 2026-09-01; current system/competency/discipline tables.

Physiology, GFR — StatPearls: PGE2/PGI2 dilate afferent arteriole; NSAIDs cause afferent constriction.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Vomiting lowers effective circulating volume, increasing dependence on prostaglandin-supported afferent dilation. Ibuprofen blocks COX, removes this afferent vasodilatory support, lowers glomerular capillary pressure, and reduces GFR.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Volume depletion itself can activate angiotensin II and cause efferent constriction, but that response tends to preserve glomerular pressure. The NSAID-specific event that explains the new GFR decline is loss of prostaglandin-mediated afferent dilation.
